name: Le Méridien Vienna
positioning: Art-filled design hotel by Vienna's Ringstrasse in the Cultural Quarter, combining a 1960s building with an 1860 palais, 200 meters from the State Opera
best_for: Travelers who want to walk to the State Opera and Vienna's museums
Art lovers who want a hotel that exhibits contemporary art

facts.text: The hotel sits by the Ringstrasse in Vienna's Cultural Quarter, close to the State Opera.
The State Opera is 200 meters from the hotel.
The hotel opened in 2003 in a combination of a 1960s building and a palais from 1860.
Le Méridien Vienna permanently exhibits works by Vienna's most promising artists.
The hotel has a library where guests can read among works of art.
Room views fall on the Ringstrasse, Schillerplatz, or the courtyard.
The Burggarten lies right in front of the hotel, for jogging.
The indoor pool in the John Harris Executive Club is heated all year.
Restaurant YOU. has a terrace on the Wiener Ringstrasse.
The Sala Terrena breakfast restaurant is a bright, greenery-filled setting.
Children are given a complimentary toy and a Discovery Guide on arrival.

highlights.text: Hotel guests get complimentary access to the Kunsthalle Wien contemporary art museum by showing their room key card.
Each headboard is a glass panel etched with an iconically Viennese image, such as a coffee cup or a horse from the Spanish Riding School, that doubles as a lamp.
The John Harris Executive Club at the hotel has fitness facilities, a pool, a whirlpool and a sauna landscape.
The Rooftop Terrace Suite looks over Vienna and the tranquil Schiller Park and has two spacious rooms.
Rooftop Terrace rooms come with their own terrace.

considerations.text: The hotel does not accept cash payments anywhere in the hotel; major credit and debit cards are accepted.
Rooms do not have a fridge.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Le Méridien Vienna
